about.storyHeading: I didn't set out to be a wedding planner. But I kept being the person everyone asked.
about.storyParagraphs:
I planned my first wedding at 23 — my sister's, because she asked, and I couldn't say no. I had no idea what I was doing. But I discovered something that day: I love the quiet machinery behind a big, emotional event. The spreadsheets, the phone calls, the 2am worries about whether the florist got the right shade of cream. I love all of it.

Nine years later, I've planned over 120 weddings across Ottawa, the Gatineau Hills, the Ottawa Valley, and beyond. I've worked in grand ballrooms and barns and backyards and on the shore of a lake at sunset. Every single one was different, and every single one taught me something I bring to the next.

But the thing that hasn't changed — and won't — is that I do this personally. I'm not building an agency. I'm not training junior planners to run weddings on my behalf. When you hire me, you get me. My phone number. My attention. My obsession with the details you care about and the ones you haven't thought of yet.

If that's the kind of relationship you want with your planner — not a vendor, but someone who becomes part of your story — then I think we'll work well together.

philosophyItems.title: Your wedding should feel like you
philosophyItems.body: Not like a Pinterest board, not like the wedding I did last month, not like what's trendy. I start every relationship by understanding who you are as a couple — then we build a day that reflects that, not a template.

philosophyItems.title: Details are not details — they’re the experience
philosophyItems.body: The difference between a good wedding and a great one isn't the big things. It's whether the bar opens on time, whether the grandmother can hear the vows, whether there's a plan when it rains. I obsess over these so you don't have to.

philosophyItems.title: Your planner should be a person, not a brand
philosophyItems.body: I deliberately keep my calendar small. When you hire me, I'm not handing you to an associate. I'm the one at your rehearsal, the one on my phone with your florist at 6am, the one making sure your day runs.

philosophyItems.title: Calm is a service
philosophyItems.body: The most valuable thing I provide isn't a spreadsheet or a vendor list — it's the feeling of knowing someone competent is handling everything. Your family should enjoy the day. You should enjoy the day. I'll handle the rest.

getServices.name: Full-Service Planning
getServices.shortDescription: From the first Pinterest board to the last toast — I handle every detail so you can be fully present on your day.
getServices.fullDescription: This is the most comprehensive offering. We start together 12–18 months out and I walk every step with you — venue scouting, vendor curation, budget management, design direction, timeline creation, and day-of coordination. You get my personal cell phone, weekly check-ins, and a planner who knows your wedding inside and out by the time the doors open.
getServices.imageAlt: Elegant wedding reception with floral arrangements and candlelit table settings

getServices.name: Partial Planning
getServices.shortDescription: You have the vision and some pieces in place — I fill the gaps, tighten the timeline, and make sure nothing falls through.
getServices.fullDescription: For couples who are 4–8 months out and have already booked a venue and some vendors but need professional help pulling it all together. I review what you have, identify gaps, recommend trusted vendors for remaining categories, build your production timeline, and coordinate the day itself.
getServices.imageAlt: Wedding table centerpiece with white flowers and candles

getServices.name: Day-Of Coordination
getServices.shortDescription: You planned it all — now let someone else run it. I take over the logistics so you and your family can enjoy the day.
getServices.fullDescription: For couples who have planned everything themselves and want a professional to execute. I step in 6–8 weeks before the wedding, review all your contracts and plans, build the master timeline, confirm all vendors, and run the rehearsal and wedding day so you can be a guest at your own wedding.
getServices.imageAlt: Outdoor wedding ceremony with floral arch and white chairs

getFaqItems.question: How many weddings do you take per year?
getFaqItems.answer: I intentionally limit my calendar to 12–15 weddings per year so that every couple gets the level of personal attention they deserve. Once we begin working together, you're not handed off to an associate — you get me, from our first meeting to the last dance.

getFaqItems.question: What makes you different from a wedding planning agency?
getFaqItems.answer: I am not an agency. I don't have a team of junior coordinators who learn on your wedding. Every plan I build, every vendor I call, every timeline I write — that's me, personally. If that's the kind of relationship you want with your planner, we'll work well together.

getFaqItems.question: Do you only work in Ottawa?
getFaqItems.answer: I'm based in Ottawa and most of my weddings are in the Ottawa–Gatineau region and Eastern Ontario. I do take on a limited number of weddings elsewhere in Ontario and Quebec — get in touch and we can talk about the specifics.

getFaqItems.question: What service levels do you offer?
getFaqItems.answer: Three: Full-Service Planning (start to finish, 12–18 months out), Partial Planning (you've started but need help pulling it together, 4–8 months out), and Day-Of Coordination (you've planned it and want a professional to run the day). You can see the details on the Services page.

getFaqItems.question: How much do your services cost?
getFaqItems.answer: Pricing depends on the scope of your wedding, the timeline, and the service level you choose. Full-service planning starts at $6,500, partial planning at $3,200, and day-of coordination at $1,800. After our initial consultation I'll give you a detailed, transparent quote — no surprises.

getFaqItems.question: Do you work with specific vendors?
getFaqItems.answer: I have a network of vendors I trust deeply — florists, photographers, caterers, calligraphers, and more — but I never force anyone on you. If you have vendors you love, I'm happy to work with them. My job is to build the right team for your wedding, not to check boxes on a preferred list.

getFaqItems.question: When should we reach out?
getFaqItems.answer: Ideally 12–18 months before your wedding for full-service planning, though I've taken on shorter timelines when the fit is right. For partial planning or day-of coordination, 4–8 months out is ideal. That said — if you're getting married next month and feeling overwhelmed, still reach out. If I can't help, I'll point you to someone who can.

getFaqItems.question: What happens after we first get in touch?
getFaqItems.answer: I'll reply within two business days to set up a free, no-pressure consultation — usually a video call or a coffee if you're in Ottawa. We talk about your vision, your timeline, and what you're looking for. If it feels right for both of us, I send a proposal. If it doesn't, I'll tell you honestly.

getProcessSteps.title: We Start With You
getProcessSteps.description: No templates, no packages first. Our first conversation is about your story, your priorities, and what you want the day to feel like — not just look like.

getProcessSteps.title: A Plan Built Around Your Day
getProcessSteps.description: I build a custom plan for your wedding — not a generic checklist. Every timeline, vendor choice, and design decision serves the specific experience you want to create.

getProcessSteps.title: You Talk to Me, Always
getProcessSteps.description: No account managers, no junior associates, no being passed around. My couples have my personal number. Questions get answered by the person who knows your wedding inside and out.

getProcessSteps.title: I Sweat the Details
getProcessSteps.description: Contracts, logistics, vendor coordination, floor plans, contingency plans — the unglamorous machinery that makes a wedding feel effortless. That's my job, not yours.

getProcessSteps.title: You Enjoy Your Day
getProcessSteps.description: When the day comes, you are a guest at your own wedding. I'm already there, three steps ahead, making sure everything happens exactly as we planned — and handling whatever we didn't.
